text: Welcome to Keyrus AI Agents,
inside Keyrus AI Studio.
Three agents, one delivery lifecycle.
From the first meeting to go-live —
powered by AI.
Every agent supports a different phase of
an Anaplan engagement, so the question is:
what do you need to do right now?
If you need to UNDERSTAND,
you start with the Discovery Agent —
it captures and structures client needs from
meetings and source files:
recapping meetings, capturing requirements,
cross-checking client inputs and building user stories.
Once the needs are clear and you
need to DESIGN, the Anaplan SA Co-Builder
Agent turns those requirements into an Anaplan
design — creating the architecture,
defining modules and formulas,
working with an existing model and helping
you build directly in Anaplan.
And when the model is already built
and you need to EXPLAIN or TEST
it, the Anaplan Model Knowledge Agent explains
and documents that build —
explaining the UX and its functionality,
tracing the backend logic,
generating test scripts and producing KT and
client guides.
That last one is the most complete of the three —
and it's the one we'll dive into now.
So let's meet the Anaplan Model Knowledge Agent.
This agent sits on top of an
already-built Anaplan model and its interface.
It ingests the backend and UX metadata
just once, and from there it answers
functional and technical questions and generates deliverables:
test scripts, client-facing user guides,
and knowledge transfer documents.
Use it whenever you need to understand
or document a model that's already built
— what a page does,
what's behind a button,
which modules it uses,
or how data flows between modules and
actions.
Getting started is simple.
You upload the six mandatory files together,
at the start of the conversation.
These files come from an extraction script
inside the QA app —
which you'll find in the Tools section
of the platform.
Once uploaded, you never need to upload
them again — the agent reuses them
throughout the whole conversation.
Once uploaded the files,
we ask it to generate the test
scripts for a UX or a whole
Anaplan category.
We are asked once whether there's anything
particular to consider and whether to keep
the default test types or use others.
In seconds, it returns a downloadable Excel
with the test cases —
and it keeps adding to that same
file, one category at a time.
It also answers questions about the model's
global backend structure.
We can ask which module is referenced
the most in the model,
what a specific module references or is
referenced by, which actions touch a module,
or where a module's data ultimately comes
from, tracing both formulas and actions.
Also, it can generate a dependent tree
for module references and build a schema
showing references in and out.
And when it's time to document,
we can ask it to generate a
user guide for a section,
or a full training document for the
whole model.
The agent generates a knowledge transfer document
in Word format with a global architecture
overview — purpose, overall architecture,
data flows, terminology, rules —
generated once per session,
plus per-category sections naming the real backend
modules and actions behind each page.
And that's just part of it.
The agent brings nine key capabilities:
module and page discovery,
functional and technical explanations,
test script generation and deep-dives,
user guides, knowledge transfer documents,
backend structure queries, a fully interactive Q&A
session, and optional visual context from PDFs
or images.
Inside the agent you'll also find related
prompts — suggestions designed for exactly what
you're doing, for every use case.
Explain, test and document a complete Anaplan
model — all in one agent,
with Anaplan Model Knowledge.
